title: clean_span default reads pt.max_span before max_span is loaded
detail: clean_span's fallback evaluates pt.max_span while it is still the constructor default 0; max_span is assigned on the next line. The intended fallback-to-loaded-max never takes effect.
recommended_fix: Load and assign pt.max_span first, then read pt.max_span as the clean_span default.

title: RunState.bootstrap never passes balance to PacketFlow
evidence:
+	s.flow = PacketFlow.new(p_catalogs)
+func _init(p_catalogs: GameCatalogs = null, p_balance: BalanceData = null) -> void:
detail: PacketFlow is constructed with catalogs only, so its balance is null. ms_per_tick, default_lane_weights, and strain/crit thresholds all fall back to hardcoded defaults instead of BalanceData.
recommended_fix: Construct as PacketFlow.new(p_catalogs, p_balance) so the flow honors tuned balance values.

title: CrisisEngine.evaluate takes concrete ScriptedDirector, not the base CrisisDirector
evidence:
+func evaluate(tick: int, _topology: TopologySnapshot, _flow: PacketFlow,
+			  era_id: int, director: ScriptedDirector) -> CrisisReport:
+## base type; swapping impls is config (ADR-7).
detail: evaluate is hard-coded to the MVP impl type, so the advertised substitutable seam (base type, ADR-7, V2 AiAuditorDirector) cannot actually be passed here.
recommended_fix: Type the director parameter as CrisisDirector and call through the base interface.

title: SET_JUNCTION_POLICY enum value has no command class, validator, or applier
detail: The enum declares SET_JUNCTION_POLICY but no matching cmd subclass exists and TopologyGraph._validate/_apply never match it, so any such command is always rejected as unknown.
recommended_fix: Either implement the junction-policy command end-to-end or remove the dead enum value.

title: QUEUE_DROP_DEPTH comment says oldest drops, but code drops newest (tail)
evidence:
+const QUEUE_DROP_DEPTH: int = 20      # per-pipe FIFO backlog before oldest drops
+				if idx_in_lane > QUEUE_DROP_DEPTH:
+					_drop(p, &"queue_overflow", arrived)
detail: backlog is spawn-ordered (oldest first); idx_in_lane counts oldest-to-newest, so idx>20 drops the tail packets. The comment claims the oldest drops, contradicting the implemented tail-drop.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment to 'newest drops (tail-drop)', or implement head-drop if that was intended.

title: _validate_set_weights describes a never-drop-class zero-lane check that is absent
evidence:
+	# a lane carrying a never-drop class may not be zeroed. The never-drop check
+	# needs the active packet classes on the pipe — validated here against the
+	# catalog's loss_tol=None types present in the active era.
+	var w: Vector3i = sw.weights
+	if w.x < 0 or w.y < 0 or w.z < 0:
+		return EditResult.rejected(&"negative_weight")
+	return EditResult.applied()
detail: The comment promises validation that a lane carrying a never-drop class is not zeroed, but the body only rejects negative weights; the never-drop guard is not implemented.
recommended_fix: Either implement the never-drop-class lane check or delete the comment claiming it is validated here.

title: _pick_dst accepts a mode argument it never uses
evidence:
+static func _pick_dst(sinks: Array, weights: Array[int], src_id: int,
+					  mode: int, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> int:
+	return _weighted_pick(cand, cand_w, rng)
detail: mode is plumbed in (spec.selection_rule.mode) but the body always does a weighted pick; ROUND_ROBIN is silently treated as WEIGHTED_RANDOM, contradicting the multi-mode design.
recommended_fix: Branch on mode (e.g., real round-robin cursor) or drop the unused parameter and document single-mode support.

title: NetNode.utilization_units is never updated; utilization_pct() always returns 0
evidence:
+var utilization_units: int = 0             # current load (updated by PacketFlow)
+func utilization_pct() -> int:
+	# Integer percent (ADR-10); throughput 0 -> 0 (guards division).
+	if throughput_units <= 0:
+		return 0
+	return (utilization_units * 100) / throughput_units
+		var load: int = int(_node_load.get(nid, 0))
+		var pct: int = (load * 100) / n.throughput_units
detail: PacketFlow tracks load in a private _node_load dict and never writes node.utilization_units, so the field and utilization_pct() are stuck at 0; the fingerprint's 'util' is meaningless.
recommended_fix: Write the resolved load onto node.utilization_units each tick, or remove the dead field/method.

title: Surge-window accumulators are never reset between surges
evidence:
+	if in_surge:
+		surge_delivered += report.delivered
+		surge_dropped += report.dropped
+		var surge_total: int = surge_delivered + surge_dropped
+		var surge_uptime: int = 100 if surge_total <= 0 else (surge_delivered * 100) / surge_total
+func reset_window() -> void:
+	surge_delivered = 0
+	surge_dropped = 0
+	_prev_in_surge = false
detail: reset_window exists but is never called in core, so a second surge's win check blends stats with the first surge, corrupting the per-surge win condition.
recommended_fix: Call reset_window() at surge start (when in_surge becomes true) so each surge is judged independently.

title: Upgrade validation skips the span<=tier.max_span check that draw enforces
evidence:
+func _validate_upgrade(cmd: Command) -> EditResult:
+	var up: Command.UpgradePipeCmd = cmd as Command.UpgradePipeCmd
+	var p: NetPipe = _pipes.get(up.pipe_id)
+	var cost: int = Economy.draw_cost(p.span_tiles, tier.cost_per_tile)
+	if economy != null and not economy.can_afford(cost):
+		return EditResult.rejected(&"over_budget")
+	return EditResult.applied()
+	if span > tier.max_span:
+		return EditResult.rejected(&"span_exceeds_tier")    # E1.1 span-limit
detail: Draw rejects span exceeding the tier max, but upgrade never re-checks against the target tier's max_span, allowing a pipe to be moved to a too-short tier.
recommended_fix: Add the span <= tier.max_span guard in _validate_upgrade using the new tier.

title: IN_FLIGHT_CAP constant is declared but never enforced
detail: The cap is defined but no code reads it; the packets array grows unbounded, so the intended overflow protection is absent.
recommended_fix: Either enforce the cap (drop/recycle on exceed) or remove the unused constant.

title: ROLLING_WINDOW comment misstates the window as 10s at 10Hz
evidence:
+const ROLLING_WINDOW: int = 100      # recent-uptime window in ticks (~10s at 10Hz)
+var logic_hz: int = 20                       # ADR-2 fixed logic tick
detail: At the fixed 20 Hz tick, 100 ticks is 5 seconds, not 10s; and the rate is 20 Hz, not 10 Hz. The comment contradicts the actual tick rate.

title: command.gd header references instance_from_dict, which is never defined
evidence:
+## Subclasses are inner classes off the `Command` base; use the `type` field to
+## dispatch, or `instance_from_dict` / typed casts.
detail: The class doc suggests deserializing via instance_from_dict, but no such function exists anywhere in the file.
recommended_fix: Implement instance_from_dict or drop the reference from the header comment.

title: lane_caps[lane] = cap writes a local array that is never read again
detail: lane_caps is a per-pipe local; after the lane loop no code reads it, so writing the residual cap back has no effect.
recommended_fix: Delete the dead write or use the residual capacities downstream.

title: Latency for packets delivered this tick is not accrued before accounting
evidence:
+	for p: Packet in packets:
+		if p.delivered or p.dropped:
+			continue
+		p.accrued_latency_ms += ms_per_tick
+		survivors.append(p)
detail: Packets delivered during the serve loop are skipped by the latency loop, so the delivery tick's ms_per_tick is never added; avg_latency_ms undercounts every delivered packet by one tick.
recommended_fix: Accrue ms_per_tick for delivered/dropped packets before moving them to the arrived list.
